page: Microsoft Azure FX4mds_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the FXmdsv2 family. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, it features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture. The processor operates at a high base clock speed of 4.2 GHz and is equipped with a substantial 260 MB L3 cache. The server is provisioned with 84.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 21.0 GB per core. It also includes 236 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is premium storage capable.

In benchmark testing, the FX4mds_v2 exhibits strong single-core capabilities, achieving a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2262.0 and strong single-threaded performance in gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, due to its low physical core count of 2, multi-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a multi-core stress-ng score of 4441.27 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression score of 28.5 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth tests show average cached read speeds of 345.52 GB/sec, but uncached large-block read and write speeds fall into the weaker tier. Database operations and Redis SET operations perform at average levels, with Redis handling 6.34 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the FX4mds_v2 offers a specialized hardware profile that prioritizes high clock speed and massive memory density per core over raw multi-threaded compute power. This makes it a highly qualitative choice for workloads that are constrained by memory capacity or single-thread execution speed rather than parallel processing. It is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, relational database hosting, caching layers, and single-threaded data processing tasks. It is less optimal for highly parallelized workloads, software compilation, or large-scale LLM inference, where its limited physical core count and lack of GPU acceleration present clear performance tradeoffs.
